name: Vauxhall / Opel
description: Vauxhall / Opel over a generic OBD-II dongle, on 11-bit/500k High Speed GMLAN. Built for the GM Global A era (Astra K, Insignia B, Mokka X, Zafira C -- roughly 2010-2019). Global A does NOT speak plain UDS: fault codes are GMW3110 ReadDiagnosticInformation (0xA9), clear is 0x04 and identification is 0x1A, so the scan ladders both dialects and reports which one answered. Powertrain sits at 0x7E0/0x7E1 (response +8); body/chassis modules use GM's own 0x24x block (response +0x400). Low-Speed GMLAN (single-wire, pin 1) carries most comfort modules and is NOT reachable through any standard dongle. 2019+ Vauxhalls are PSA/Stellantis platforms, not GM -- use the Peugeot profile for those. Read-only apart from a confirm-gated fault clear and the Transmission Adaptive Values Learn -- the one routine the harness runs itself, over GMW3110 DeviceControl, from frames recovered out of GM's own dealer database and never yet seen on a wire.

panel.title: GMLAN module scan (OBD dongle)
panel.hint: Astra K 1.4T auto: TCM is at 0x7E2, not the textbook 0x7E1. Scan reads every module's fault memory. 'Gearbox analyse' is the 6T35 job -- calibration, GM-named faults (not SAE-generic), live block, clutch map, and the clutch adapt cells. 'Engine analyse' is the same job on the engine controller at 0x7E0, built for the Astra J VXR A20NFT out of GM's own E39A dealer data -- and unlike the gearbox that data has never been checked against a car, so read its applicability table before believing any of its numbers. Find modules / Software versions still sit here. Everything on this panel is read-only except the two adaptive-learn buttons: 'Learn preflight' reads whether the gearbox would accept a Transmission Adaptive Values Learn and sends nothing, and 'Adaptive values learn' actually runs it. That routine has NEVER been run on a car -- its frames are a confirmed static decode of GM's own dealer database and nothing more -- so rehearse it in Simulate mode first, where every failure path can be watched. Ignition ON.
panel.scanBusy: Reading the Vauxhall over GMLAN (UDS dialect first, then GMW3110)...

actions.label: Find modules
actions.busy: Sweeping the GMLAN diagnostic address blocks...
actions.title: Find this car's modules
actions.hint: Probes every address in the powertrain block (0x7E0-0x7E7, reply +8) and GM's body/chassis block (0x240-0x25F, reply +0x400) and reports which ones answer, which dialect they answered in, and what they call themselves. This is how you build a verified module map for a model nobody has published one for. Read-only.

actions.label: Software versions
actions.busy: Reading each module's flashed software identification...
actions.title: What software is in this car
actions.hint: Asks every module that answers for the calibration it is actually running: End Model Part Number, Base Model Part Number, Boot Software Part Number and Software Module Identifiers 01-10, each with its two-character alpha code, plus the date it was last programmed and the tester code that programmed it. Part numbers come out of GMW3110 as 4-byte binary and are shown as the decimal a parts catalogue quotes. This is the step before asking whether an update exists -- including a gearbox recalibration: take these numbers to the manufacturer's programming system and compare against what it offers for the VIN. Read-only. The harness reads calibrations, it does not write them.

actions.label: Gearbox analyse
actions.busy: Reading the TCM -- calibration, faults, live...
actions.title: Astra K 6T35 gearbox
actions.hint: Finds the TCM (0x7E2 on this Astra K, 0x7E1 fallback), reads the calibration part numbers, reads faults with GM 6T35/6T40 names (P2723 is the 1-2-3-4 clutch, not 'Shift Solenoid E'), reads the live block (fluid temp, selector, range switch, shaft speeds, commanded gear, gear ratio, TCC slip and the fast-learn readiness state), asks for the clutch adapt cells, and writes a worksheet that maps codes onto clutches. Read-only. Signals named from the GDS2 dealer data but never yet seen on this car are marked as such rather than shown as fact.

actions.label: Engine analyse
actions.busy: Reading the ECM -- identification, faults, live block...
actions.title: Astra J VXR A20NFT engine
actions.hint: Finds the ECM at 0x7E0, reads its identification and calibration part numbers, reads faults with GM's own wording out of the dealer dictionary, reads a curated 35-parameter live block (rpm, load, coolant, intake air, MAF, throttle demanded vs actual, both fuel trims, commanded lambda, both lambda sensors, rail pressure desired vs actual, boost desired vs actual, wastegate and bypass command, ignition timing, knock retard, cam position desired vs actual on both cams, and the misfire counters) and writes a worksheet. THE PARAMETER LIST CAME FROM GM'S GDS2 DEALER DATABASE AND HAS NEVER BEEN CONFIRMED ON THIS ENGINE -- not one of these has been asked of an A20NFT. GM's list is its shared 'E39 4-cylinder' set, so expect a fair number to come back NRC 31 (request out of range); that split is reported as the applicability table and is the most useful thing a first run produces. There are no pass/fail thresholds in GM's data, so nothing here judges a reading -- it reports the number and names the divergence. Read-only: no clear, no coding, no adaptation, and the 70 DeviceControl frames GM's data carries are listed for information and never transmitted.

actions.label: Gearbox live
actions.busy: Reading the gearbox and engine live values...
actions.title: Vauxhall gearbox + engine live
actions.hint: Astra K verified block on the TCM at 0x7E2 (DID 1940 fluid temp, 194F selector, 1951 range switch, 1941/1942 shaft speeds) -- the same 1940@7E2 mapping Torque ships as 'Pontiac / GM / Opel / Vauxhall'. Falls back to the OBDb 0x7E1 04FE/5503/5504 set on cars that actually have it. Fluid temp is also the Fast Learn precondition, and 2823 reports the module's own readiness through GDS2's 17-state table. Clutch adapt cells, line pressure and slip are named by the GDS2 data now, but nothing is shown for them until they have answered on this car.

actions.label: Learn preflight
actions.busy: Reading the gearbox's readiness -- temperature, selector, engine speed, module state...
actions.title: Adaptive values learn -- preflight
actions.hint: Reads everything the adaptive values learn is gated on and sends nothing: the live transmission fluid temperature, the module's own 17-state readiness parameter (22 28 23) decoded through GDS2's own table, and each of the three preconditions GDS2's condition set checks -- selector in Park or Neutral, fluid above the threshold, engine running. Service 0x22 only. If it reports a blocker, fix that first: the module names what it is waiting for, and reading it costs nothing. The fluid temperature it prints is the number you will be asked to acknowledge before the learn will start.

actions.label: Adaptive values learn
actions.busy: Running the adaptive values learn -- do not switch off...
actions.title: Transmission Adaptive Values Learn (T76 / 6T35)
actions.hint: Runs GM's Transmission Adaptive Values Learn on the gearbox controller: GMW3110 DeviceControl on CPID 0x30 at 0x7E2, with TesterPresent held through the routine and the device control released on every path out, including failures. THIS HAS NEVER BEEN RUN ON A CAR. The frames were recovered by static analysis of the GDS2 dealer database, re-derived independently from raw file offsets and reproduced across five separately built deliverables -- which is the strongest evidence a static decode can carry, and is not the same as evidence from a car. Two things are still open: whether the module demands SecurityAccess, and whether a Bluetooth dongle can hold the channel for the length of the routine. The dangerous outcome is not a refusal but an interruption: the routine clears the gearbox's adaptive cells when it starts and only writes new ones when it finishes. The car is driven against its own brakes with the engine running -- chock the wheels, park brake on, foot on the service brake, everyone clear. Run the preflight first; you will be asked to confirm, and to type back the fluid temperature you can see. In Simulate mode the whole exchange runs against a simulated module, and the scenario picker replays each failure path.
